excerpt: Let an AI model use a real iPhone with a $7 ESP32. Just the phone and the board: no computer, no jailbreak.
Type a goal (for example "Open Settings and go to Wi-Fi") and press Start.
the agent leaves its own app, opens Clock, types the time into the wheel, ticks the days and saves.
It runs in the background while it works; the Dynamic Island shows what it is doing.
Siri, Shortcuts, widgets and Control Center can run saved tasks.
Any OpenAI-compatible vision endpoint works (vLLM, SGLang, llama.cpp, Ollama, cloud APIs).
The app lists the endpoint's models for you to choose one explicitly; you can also enter a model ID, and set a separate planner and actor model.
The prompts are plain text in prompts/ and bundled with the app: edit them, rebuild, done.
Give Me a Brain — enter your model endpoint and key (stored in the Keychain)
Setup walks through four steps and checks each one itself
Let Me Use the Pointer — turn on AssistiveTouch; the app calibrates the pointer by itself.
A lost board, hotspot or mirroring link pauses the run and resumes it from the same step.
Every run is kept on the phone: replay it step by step with the taps and swipes drawn on top.
Export the screenshots, actions and saved annotations from Runs → open a run → ⋯ → Export trace for analysis by another agent.
Always build with flash.sh: it applies the BLE buffer sizes in hardware/hid_bridge/nimble_cfg.h.
A free Apple ID can sign it (re-sign every 7 days).
Debugging without the phone app: hardware/tools/board_test.py plays the app over BLE from a Mac
New: the computer is gone. The board is now the AirPlay receiver and the mouse, and the agent runs in an iPhone app on the same phone.
USB-C models plug in directly; Lightning models need a Lightning to USB Camera Adapter. The phone powers the board.
